exact_items: Define `route_target` as the canonical navigation-and-focus contract.
Define `OpenSubject` as the canonical identity-native source-open contract.
Keep `OpenFile` as the path-based editor contract only.

State the resolution chain directly: `route_target` may land on a surface that then invokes `OpenSubject`; `OpenSubject` may resolve to `OpenFile`; `OpenSubject` may resolve to a transient `generated://<artifact_id>` source buffer
The three contracts are now distinct: `route_target` = navigation; `OpenSubject` = identity-native source open; `OpenFile` = path-based editor open
notes: The three-contract split is the key architectural decision: route_target owns navigation, OpenSubject owns identity-native source open, OpenFile owns path-based editor open. If route_target carries source-buffer realization details it will bloat. If OpenSubject carries panel/tab/shell destination semantics it collapses back into a second route contract.
resume_url sits on the route_target side (restores app navigation context), NOT the OpenSubject side.

exact_items: Keep the intent vocabulary controlled and small: `open_source`; `open_preview`; `open_review`
Keep resolver-support metadata out of the contract.

State the resolution rule directly: `OpenSubject(subject_id = doc:...)` resolves to workspace-backed source opening; `OpenSubject(subject_id = artifact:...)` resolves to real document source if one exists; otherwise it resolves to transient `generated://<artifact_id>` source opening

`OpenSubject` does not carry: `project_id`, `thread_id`, `run_id`, `tab_id`, `panel_id`, `inspector_target`, `origin_surface`, `source_kind`, `backing_document_id`, `last_saved_path`, `generated://<artifact_id>`, preview persistence state, transport mode
notes: OpenSubject minimum field set: subject_id + open_intent (open_source | open_preview | open_review). Shell/scope (project_id, thread_id, etc.) belong to route_target not OpenSubject. Persistence/provenance (backing_document_id, source_kind, last_saved_path) belong to storage records. Transport/open realization (generated://) belongs to the resolver.

exact_items: `FileManager.md` still makes `OpenFile` look like the universal open/navigation primitive.
`FileManager.md` should stay focused on path-based editor realization and should not become the owner of cross-surface identity navigation just because `OpenFile` is important there.
`assistant-chat-design.md` and `FinalGUISpec.md` already treat `open_source` as a real action, but the action still lacks a contract owner.
notes: FileManager.md must be updated to clearly scope OpenFile as path-based editor only. The doc must reference Contracts_V0 for OpenSubject and route_target rather than implying OpenFile handles all navigation.

exact_items: The canonical minimum field set is: `target_kind`; `project_id`; one canonical target selector (`subject_id` OR `object_kind` + `object_id`)
`project_id` is required. Exactly one canonical target selector is required.

What is NOT a base `route_target` field: `usage_event_ref`, `wizard_id`, `wizard_step`, `message_id`, `artifact_id`, `document_id`, `workflow_run_id`, `scheduler_pass_id`, `safe_point_id`, `remediation_root_id`, `line`, `range`, per-surface state (`active_subview`, compare target, panel layout, browser tab state, widget layout)
canonical_replacement_hints: object_kind + object_id for wizard_id, message_id, usage_event, scheduler_pass_id, safe_point_id, remediation_root_id
notes: route_target is now bounded. artifact_id and document_id normalize into subject_id. wizard_id, message_id, scheduler_pass_id, safe_point_id, remediation_root_id normalize into object_kind/object_id. usage_event_ref normalizes into object_kind=usage_event. wizard_step is sub-selection (not base route identity).
